hyperparameters.note: TOFU's own literature-standard default config, not modified

interpretation: CROSS-DATASET COMPARISON, first real data point. Running GA on TOFU with TOFU's OWN literature-standard config (10 epochs, lr=1e-5, unmodified) produces the SAME catastrophic collapse pattern found on BioMistral-7B/BioUnlearn-Bench: model_utility crashes to exactly 0.0 by epoch 4 and stays there for the remaining 6 epochs, extraction_strength hits a floor, forget probability goes to numerical zero (unbounded negative loss, -50.06 final, same failure mode as our own -222 case just less extreme). This is genuinely important: it means GA's aggressive collapse is NOT a BioUnlearn-Bench-specific artifact -- the same method collapses on the field's own standard benchmark at its own standard settings too. BUT this also means the standard TOFU config is not a fair 'successful baseline' comparison point either -- a meaningful cross-dataset comparison (does GA fail differently/worse on BioUnlearn-Bench specifically) requires a NON-collapsed, gentler GA run on TOFU too, matching the same step-count-based gentle-tuning philosophy already applied to BioMistral (few steps, not epochs). Next: retry with a much lower step budget on TOFU to get a genuinely comparable, non-degenerate baseline point.
